### [LearnWorlds vs Teachable: A Hands-On Comparison (2026)](https://athemes.com/reviews/learnworlds-vs-teachable/)

**Published:** April 7, 2021
**Author:** Rosie Greaves

**Content:**

With so many online course platforms on the market, it can be challenging to decipher which is best for your needs. So, to shed some light, we’re comparing two players in the e-learning industry: [LearnWorlds](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds) vs [Teachable](https://athemes.com/go/teachable).

Hopefully, by the end of this review, you’ll be better positioned to decide which (if either) is the better fit for your venture.

Whichever you pick, if your site runs on WordPress, [Sydney](https://athemes.com/theme/sydney/) is our fast, customizable business theme, with [starter sites](https://athemes.com/sydney-demos/) to build on.

Let’s start by exploring their key similarities and differences, then jump into comparing the features and prices.

LearnWorlds and Teachable are two of the most popular online course platforms, and the best one depends on what you are building. LearnWorlds is the more powerful platform, with interactive video, advanced quizzes, and a full website builder. Teachable is simpler and faster to launch, with native mobile apps and an easy way to sell different types of products.

On price, the two now start close together. LearnWorlds Starter is $24 a month and Teachable Starter is $29 a month, both billed annually. Neither has a free plan anymore, though LearnWorlds offers a 30-day free trial and Teachable a 7-day trial. Watch the fees: LearnWorlds charges $5 per enrollment on Starter while Teachable charges 7.5%, with both dropping to 0% on higher plans.

Choose LearnWorlds if you want the deepest course-creation tools, assessments, and community features. Choose Teachable if you want the quickest, simplest way to launch and sell, plus native mobile apps. Here is how they compare at a glance.

| Feature | LearnWorlds | Teachable |
|---|---|---|
| Starting price | $24/mo (Starter, billed annually) | $29/mo (Starter, billed annually) |
| Free plan | No (30-day free trial) | No (7-day free trial) |
| Transaction fees | $5 per enrollment on Starter; 0% on higher plans | 7.5% on Starter; 0% on higher plans |
| Cheapest 0%-fee plan | Pro Trainer, $79/mo | Builder, $69/mo |
| Course building | Interactive video, deep customization | Simple, fast to launch |
| Quizzes and assessments | Advanced (question banks, SCORM) | Basic (multiple choice) |
| Community | Yes, built-in | Yes (Communities product) |
| Native mobile app | No (browser-based) | Yes, iOS and Android |
| Certificates | Customizable | Template-based |
| Best for | Serious creators, assessments, communities | Beginners, fast launch, varied products |

#####  Table of Contents 

1. [Teachable vs LearnWorlds: their main similarities](#teachable-vs-learnworlds-their-main-similarities)
2. [Teachable vs LearnWorlds: their main differences](#teachable-vs-learnworlds-their-main-differences)
3. [LearnWorlds vs Teachable: their core features compared](#learnworlds-vs-teachable-their-core-features-compared)
4. [LearnWorlds vs Teachable: customer support and training](#learnworlds-vs-teachable-customer-support-and-training)
5. [LearnWorlds vs Teachable: pricing](#learnworlds-vs-teachable-pricing)
6. [LearnWorlds vs Teachable: final thoughts](#learnworlds-vs-teachable-final-thoughts)

## Teachable vs LearnWorlds: their main similarities

- Both Teachable and LearnWorlds enable you to offer students graded quizzing and course completion certificates.
- When you sign up for Teachable and LearnWorlds’ cheapest packages, you’re charged a transaction fee whenever you make a sale. However, if you upgrade to one of their higher-priced plans, these fees are waived.
- Both LearnWorlds and Teachable come with similar marketing features, including coupons, free courses, affiliate marketing, and various payment options.
- Both LearnWorlds and Teachable make it easy to build an online school and connect a custom domain.
- Both e-learning platforms offer free SSL certificates with all packages.
- Both offer one-on-one coaching.

## Teachable vs LearnWorlds: their main differences

- LearnWorlds allows you to create student communities, whereas Teachable doesn’t offer similar functionality.
- LearnWorlds’ course builder places a heavier focus on video content.
- LearnWorlds provides a broader range of quiz and assessment types. Whereas, Teachable limits you to multiple-choice questions.
- Both platforms reserve full white-labeling for their higher tiers. Teachable removes its branding on plans above Starter, while LearnWorlds includes white-label options on its higher plans.
- LearnWorlds offers users 24/7 support via email. Alternatively, you can telephone LearnWorlds Monday to Friday from 8:00 to 17:00 EST (UK and US numbers available) or use their live chat service. However, Teachable only provides support via email and live chat during business hours (8:00 to 20:00 EST), and live chat is available on its paid plans.
- Only LearnWorlds allows you to offer group coaching as a product. Teachable just supports 1:1 coaching.
- Neither platform offers a free plan now. Teachable has a 7-day free trial, and LearnWorlds has a 30-day free trial.

## LearnWorlds vs Teachable: their core features compared

Now, let’s see how the key features (course building, quizzing and testing, certificates, community building, marketing, and payment options) of these two e-learning platforms stack up to each other.

### Course building

The course builder is the meat of any e-learning platform. The building blocks your editor provides have a direct bearing on the kind of learning experience you create.

That said, let’s see how LearnWorlds and Teachable compare when it comes to course building features.

#### Teachable

Teachable’s [web page builder](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/360033509572-Create-Edit-Your-Pages) is incredibly easy to use. You just drag the elements you want to use and drop them wherever you want on the page. And, rest assured, your finished work will be completely responsive. It doesn’t matter what device students use to access your content; they’re sure to have a great experience!

Alternatively, you can work with a website you already have up and running by linking it with Teachable, so whether you start from scratch or pick up on a work in progress, the choice is entirely yours.

When it comes to course creation, you can use video, text, image, audio, and PDF files. Once you’re finished creating your course materials, it’s easy to import them to Dropbox, OneDrive, or Google Drive.

If you want to dig deeper into your online store’s customization, use Teachable’s [power editor](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/222807127-Power-Editor). This provides direct access to Teachable’s code, so if you have the know-how, you can make advanced edits to bring your exact vision to life.

Another nifty feature is that the text on your Teachable site automatically translates to reflect your student’s native language.

On top of that, there are plenty of course compliance tools available. This means you can require students to pass a quiz to a certain standard or complete specific lessons or modules before proceeding with the course. You can even limit the number of quiz retake attempts students can make and send an alert when students use up all their attempts.

Teachable also offers an easy-to-navigate SEO setup. This comes in handy for ensuring your online school is search engine friendly.

The sheer number of helpful drag-and-drop building blocks Teachable provides for course creation is commendable. These include:

- Banner blocks
- Text blocks
- Image with text blocks
- Curriculum blocks
- Featured courses blocks

All these blocks are self-contained, so the customizations you make to one won’t affect the others, making it incredibly easy to use and navigate.

[![Teachable course building](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-course-building-768x369.png "teachable-course-building – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-course-building.png)

#### LearnWorlds

When it comes to course creation, LearnWorlds’ focus is [video content](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-video-editor).

Within a matter of clicks, you can automatically extract an interactive transcript of your video. This comes in handy for making your video content more accessible and easier to navigate. Plus, you can add all sorts of things to your videos to make them more engaging, including titles, image overlays, links, interactions, and questions.

You can even choose and design the learning pathways students take. For instance, you can drip-feed content to them. Or, create pre-set performance thresholds to ensure students go through your course content sequentially. Alternatively, you can empower students to consume your course at whatever pace they wish, and in whichever order.

I also love that LearnWorlds’ course player enables students to highlight course content and add notes as they go through the lessons and modules. This works wonders for creating a truly interactive and engaging student experience.

[![LearnWorlds course building](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-course-building-768x369.png "learnworlds-course-building – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-course-building.png)

#### Course building, winner: Teachable

If you’re really keen on video content, LearnWorlds is the best choice for you. However, Teachable wins out in the end as the better all-around course builder with a more significant number of building blocks at your disposal.

### **Coaching**

In addition to course building, both Teachable and LearnWorlds let you add coaching functionality to your website.

#### Teachable

On all of its paid plans, Teachable allows you to [offer 1:1 teaching](https://athemes.com/go/teachable-coaching) to customers as a new product, using the existing coaching scheduling and video conference tools that integrate with Teachable.

You can add intake forms to your landing page to obtain crucial information for your appointments upfront, for example, details about your customers’ backgrounds and what they hope to gain from a coaching session.

You can also bundle coaching and courses together for a more attractive offering. For instance, more invested customers might purchase a course and a follow-up coaching session at the same time.

[![Teachable coaching](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-coaching-680x388.png "teachable-coaching – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-coaching.png)

#### LearnWorlds

In 2022, LearnWorlds also introduced [one-on-one coaching](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-coaching) and group live session features.

This enables you to offer another teaching style to monetize your audience. This goes hand-in-hand with LearnWorlds’ Calendly integration to schedule your live sessions.

[![LearnWorlds coaching](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-coaching-680x364.png "learnworlds-coaching – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-coaching.png)

#### The winner: Teachable

Teachable marginally takes the win. It’s clear that the platform considered the needs of coaches more fully. For example, intake forms help you prepare for your appointments, and the fact you can bundle coaching with courses adds more versatility.

In contrast, LearnWorlds’ coaching features feel more like a convenient add-on, though if you’re interested in coaching whole groups at a time, this is a viable go-to.

### Quizzing and testing

Quizzes are an effective and interactive way of engaging students with your course material. It also gives you and your students a chance to evaluate their progress.

So, without further ado, here are the quizzing and testing options LearnWorlds and Teachable both have to offer.

#### Teachable

You can set [graded quizzes](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/219824267#AddQuizzes), which works wonders for monitoring your student’s progress. While this is a neat feature, it’s somewhat limited.

Teachable quizzes are restricted to only multiple-choice questions and true/false responses. If you’re hoping to set students’ open assignments, this isn’t an option.

However, you can use these quizzes as a compliance measure, something students have to complete and pass before proceeding further along your course.

[![Teachable quizzing and testing](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-quizzing-and-testing-768x369.png "teachable-quizzing-and-testing – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-quizzing-and-testing.png)

#### LearnWorlds

In contrast, LearnWorlds’ testing engine is nothing short of sophisticated. You can create pretty much any quiz you want: graded, ungraded, open/closed questions, you name it, you can do it with LearnWorlds.

With LearnWorlds’ Pro plan (and higher), you can create and use a question bank. This is where you make a giant pool of questions that you can call upon to set up your quizzes. Needless to say, if you’re looking to create randomized tests, this is the easiest way to do so.

[![LearnWorlds quizzing and testing](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-quizzing-and-testing-768x369.png "learnworlds-quizzing-and-testing – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-quizzing-and-testing.png)

#### Quizzing and testing, winner: LearnWorlds

It’s plain to see that LearnWorlds offers more where quizzing and testing are concerned. Its range of quizzing options is second to none.

However, if quizzes and tests don’t form a considerable part of your course, Teachable’s offering may be substantial enough.

### Certificates

Nothing is as satisfying as hitting a milestone, and completing an online course is no exception. This is why offering students digital certificates to reward their hard work is a fabulous way of rounding off your online course creation.

Not only does this work wonders for cultivating a sense of achievement, but it also exudes professionalism, which helps to establish you as an industry authority.

#### Teachable

Teachable makes it easy to design and issue [course completion certificates](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/360004562891-Certificates-of-Completion). There are three templates to choose from, all of which lay an excellent foundation for a professional-looking certificate.

Just add your own logo, text, and signature, and voilà, you’re good to go. Alternatively, you can create your own designs from scratch.

[![Teachable certificates](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-certificates-768x431.png "teachable-certificates – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-certificates.png)

#### LearnWorlds

LearnWorlds, too, enables you to reward students with course completion certificates. You can create personalized certificates [using PDF templates](https://support.learnworlds.com/support/solutions/articles/5000665480-how-to-create-a-certificate-template-for-your-learnworlds-school) and an online PDF editor to add the user’s name and course.

Since you’re creating your own PDF docs, the design is entirely up to you. Once complete, just upload it to the LearnWorlds platform, and you’re good to go!

Unlike Teachable, LearnWorlds doesn’t officially issue course completion templates for you to edit. Still, on their blog, you’ll find several [course certificate templates](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-course-certificate) created with Canva, so this is certainly an option available to you.

Then, all that’s left is to link up a ‘completion action’ with the certificate to issue them at the right time. You can award certificates for finishing part of a course, as well as for full course completion. For example, once a student passes a quiz, this action could trigger the issuing of a certificate.

Lastly, it’s up to you whether students can share certificates on Facebook, LinkedIn, or Twitter.

[![LearnWorlds certificates](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-certificates.png "learnworlds-certificates – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-certificates.png)

#### Certificates, winner: Teachable

Both Teachable and LearnWorlds make it easy to create course completion certificates. However, Teachable makes certificate creation slightly easier with its templates.

### Community building

Establishing a community surrounding your online course is as much a marketing feature as it is an excellent way of enhancing the student experience. When you enable students to unite over your course materials, you give them a safe space to ask questions, network, and make friendships.

And who knows? Once they form personal connections with your brand at the heart of those relationships, your students are far more likely to sign up in groups for your next courses. So, with all that said, how do Teachable and LearnWorlds compare?

#### Teachable

We can reach a quick conclusion here. Teachable doesn’t offer any community-building features, you can’t even create a discussion forum on your courses. To work around this, you could open a private Facebook group that’s only available to course members.

#### LearnWorlds

With its built-in [social networking](https://support.learnworlds.com/support/solutions/articles/12000050583-community-and-groups) feature, LearnWorlds excels in this area. Here, everyone enrolled in your courses gets a public profile that represents them.

Your students can communicate and network with one another, making it easy to share their experiences, swap ideas and tips, discuss any issues, provide feedback, and communicate with the instructor.

[![LearnWorlds community building](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-community-building-768x369.png "learnworlds-community-building – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-community-building.png)

#### Community building, winner: LearnWorlds

LearnWorlds wins this round. They provide an innovative way of cultivating a sense of community and engaging students with your course content. Unfortunately, this is an area in which Teachable severely lacks.

### Marketing

Once you’ve created your course, you need to market it. You could have the best class in the world, but if no one knows about it, no one is going to buy it! This is where marketing features come in handy.

#### Teachable

Much of Teachable’s in-built marketing functionality hinges on its [affiliate marketing platform](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/219826967-School-Affiliates). This enables brand advocates to advertise your offering on their website or social media platforms. Then, anytime someone purchases your online course using your affiliate’s designated link, they’re credited for the sale and earn a commission.

This works wonders for improving your profit margins and inspiring loyalty amidst your audience. You can specify which courses are available to affiliates to market and easily manage your ambassadors’ payments while controlling what percentage the affiliate will get.

Teachable also allows you to create and promote free courses. These are often just the ticket for encouraging potential students to engage with your content before committing their hard-earned cash.

You can also generate customer coupons to make your offer more appealing.

Lastly, you can build attractive, high-converting sales pages using Teachable’s page editor, which uses the same easy to use drag-and-drop function I’ve already mentioned.

Teachable also allows you to sell digital downloads as a project. Alternatively, you could offer free resources to prospective students as a lead magnet. Examples include pdfs, e-publications, spreadsheets, and more. The platform also allows you to set custom pricing tiers for your digital downloads, allowing you to flexibly bundle what’s included in each pricing tier.

[![Teachable marketing](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-marketing-1-768x369.png "teachable-marketing-1 – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-marketing-1.png)

#### LearnWorlds

LearnWorlds also offers an [in-built affiliate marketing program](https://www.learnworlds.com/affiliates/?fp_ref=athemes) functionality that you can activate through your academy dashboard. You can set the commission you want to offer your affiliates and the referral cookie expiration period. Plus, on the Learning Center plan, affiliates can even self-register. You can also track commissions and you’ll receive in-depth analytics on your affiliates’ success.

You can also design beautiful [sales pages](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-marketing-tools) that include one-click funnels. It’s easy to create and publish opt-in forms where customers can sign up to learn more about what you’re offering.

On top of that, you can build customizable checkout experiences that instill confidence in your customers. At this point, you can upsell your products and services, enable customers to use their coupon codes, and offer shoppers course bundles and subscriptions.

LearnWorlds also allows you to sell digital products such as eBooks and PDFs through your online school and even comes with a built-in eBook builder.

[![LearnWorlds marketing](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-marketing-768x369.png "learnworlds-marketing – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-marketing.png)

#### Marketing, winner: a tie!

All in all, both LearnWorlds and Teachable’s marketing features are pretty basic. Neither offers much in terms of email marketing, but both provide coupon and landing page creation as well as simple affiliate marketing.

### Payment options

The payment options available to you have a massive bearing on your conversion rate. With that in mind, here are the payment options offered by LearnWorlds vs Teachable.

#### Teachable

Teachable provides a wide range of [flexible payment structures](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us/articles/219826827-Get-Started-with-Payments) you can offer students, including:

- Membership subscriptions
- Single, one-off payments
- Course and coaching bundles
- Payment plans

What’s more, Teachable accepts over 130 currencies via PayPal, Mobile Pay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay.

Teachable also features its own payment gateway called [teachable:pay](https://athemes.com/go/teachable-pay). Using this payment method makes you eligible for features such as automatic author and affiliate payouts, automated tax form collection, and more. It also handles the remittance of US sales tax and other digital content taxes, and you can opt for daily, weekly, or monthly payouts to your account.

[![Teachable payment options](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-payment-options-1-768x400.png "teachable-payment-options-1 – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-payment-options-1.png)

#### LearnWorlds

LearnWorlds and Teachable are somewhat similar where payment options are concerned. LeanWorlds also enables you to offer students:

- Memberships
- Subscriptions
- Course bundles
- One-off payments

LearnWorlds accepts multiple currencies and five [payment gateways](https://support.learnworlds.com/support/solutions/articles/12000027007-payment-gateways), including PayPal, Stripe, 2Checkout, Klarna, Apple and Google Pay**,** Shopify, and PagSeguro.

[![LearnWorlds payment options](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-payment-options-768x369.png "learnworlds-payment-options – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-payment-options.png)

#### Payment options, winner: Teachable

Where payment options are concerned, LearnWorlds and Teachable aren’t too different, apart from one thing: Teachable offers its own payment gateway. As this unlocks a few additional benefits, we’ve crowned Teachable the winner here (just!).

## LearnWorlds vs Teachable: customer support and training

If something goes wrong, who can you turn to? This is where customer support and training are imperative. Let’s see what both LearnWorlds and Teachable offer concerning customer care.

### Teachable

Teachable offers support during business hours via support tickets or email, (8 AM to 8 PM EST). Starter plan users and upwards can access live group coaching sessions. Here, you’re in contact with a customer success manager who will provide tailored advice on improving your courses and moving your business in the right direction.

Pro customers or higher also unlock live chat, which is available from 10 AM to 5 PM EST Monday to Friday.

Teachable gives all paying members (regardless of which paid-for plan they’re on) access to their [exclusive community](https://athemes.com/go/teachable-community), which offers industry-relevant discussion, privacy, and a space to speak freely about the intricacies of running an online business. Members automatically grouped with other users at similar stages in their business careers. As your business grows, you level up within the community too.

You also get access to Teachable’s online ‘university’ called [TeachableU](https://u.teachable.com/). Here, you’ll find several training courses and self-help guides on how to make the most out of Teachable.

Their [online knowledge base](https://support.teachable.com/hc/en-us) is brimming with tutorials, too.

[![Teachable customer support](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-customer-support-1-768x369.png "teachable-customer-support-1 – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/teachable-customer-support-1.png)

### LearnWorlds

LearnWorlds offers [24/7 support](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-contact). On top of that, if you’ve opted for the Pro Trainer plan, you’ll also receive access to the LearnWords Academy and priority email support.

Alternatively, if you’ve subscribed to the Learning Center plan, your onboarding experience is amped up a notch with two hours of premium onboarding. Here, an expert will walk you through importing courses, branding tips, getting set up, customizing your online school design, and much more.

If you don’t have time or aren’t sure how to migrate your content over to LearnWorlds, the support team can also take care of that for you.

Finally, there’s an extensive [online knowledge base](https://support.learnworlds.com/support/home) and the [LearnWorlds Academy](https://academy.learnworlds.com/), which features dozens of courses on how to create course content, boost sales, and get more leads!

[![LearnWorlds customer support](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-customer-support-768x369.png "learnworlds-customer-support – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-customer-support.png)

### Customer support and training, winner: a tie!

Both LearnWorlds and Teachable provide hands-on support teams, so should you ever get stuck, you’re never on your own. Plus, both platforms offer extensive online knowledge bases that should cover most of your questions.

Beyond this, the choice is made more difficult by both platforms having their advantages and downsides. For instance, Teachable offers live chat, whereas LearnWorlds doesn’t. On the flip side, LearnWorlds’ support is 24/7, whereas Teachable sticks to its office hours.

## LearnWorlds vs Teachable: pricing

No matter the platform you choose, ultimately, the goal is to profit with your online school. So, you’ll need to weigh up your costs and expenses.

It’s up to you to find the service that provides the best value for money, especially if you’re working on a strict budget. Here’s how LearnWorlds vs Teachable compare on pricing.

### Teachable

All of Teachable’s [pricing plans](https://athemes.com/go/teachable-pricing) boast unlimited video uploads, students**,** and hosting. You also get access to integrated payment processing, student management features, lecture comments, basic quizzes, 0% fees when you ‘sell’ free courses, and VAT (value-added tax) for EU customers.

#### Teachable pricing plans

Teachable no longer offers a free plan (it was discontinued in 2025). You can still try any plan free for 7 days, and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee. There are four paid plans, shown here at the annual rate.

#### The Starter plan

Starter is Teachable’s cheapest paid plan at $29 a month (billed annually, or $39 month to month). It carries a 7.5% transaction fee and includes:

- 1 admin user
- Up to 5 products
- Up to 100 active students
- A custom domain
- Integrated email marketing and coupons
- Community and coaching products

#### The Builder plan

Builder costs $69 a month (billed annually, or $89 month to month) and removes transaction fees entirely (0%). On top of everything in Starter, you get:

- 0% transaction fees
- Up to 10 products
- Up to 1,000 active students
- Course completion certificates
- Graded quizzes and course compliance
- An unbranded website

#### The Growth plan

Growth is the plan Teachable markets as most popular. It costs $139 a month (billed annually, or $189 month to month), keeps 0% transaction fees, and adds:

- Up to 5 admin users
- Up to 50 products
- Up to 5,000 active students
- Advanced reporting and affiliate marketing
- Upsells and advanced customization

#### The Advanced plan

Advanced is Teachable’s top creator plan at $309 a month (billed annually, or $399 month to month). It includes everything in Growth, plus higher limits (up to 100 products, 5 admins, and 10,000 active students) and priority support. Teachable also offers custom Enterprise plans above this.

### LearnWorlds

Like Teachable, there are also three [paid-for packages](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds-pricing) available, which we go into in more detail below.

#### The Starter plan

This costs $24 a month, and like Teachable, it also comes with a transaction fee. But instead of a percentage of each sale, you pay a $5 flat fee on every course enrollment.

That said, you can create as many paid-for courses as you want (you can’t make free courses on the Starter plan). You can only make three kinds of web pages with its page builder:

- Homepages
- Course catalogs
- Login pages

Starter plan users get access to exam and quizzing functionality and the eBook builder.

On top of that, you can seamlessly integrate with several third-party apps, and you get a custom web domain and SSL certificate.  You also have access to 24/5 email support.

#### The Pro Trainer plan

LearnWorlds’ Pro Trainer package is the next step up and will cost you $79 a month. With this program, you get everything in the Starter plan, plus:

- Five admin- or instructor-level users
- Unlimited free and paid courses and landing pages
- The complete page builder
- Access to assessments and certificates, as well as live classes and webinars
- 0% transaction fees
- Offer customers installment plans, subscriptions, and memberships
- Create a fully customizable checkout page
- Customize your course player
- Premium integrations

#### The Learning Center plan

LearnWorlds’ most expensive plan comes in at $249 a month. This entitles you to everything in the previous two programs, as well as:

- 20 admin- or instructor-level users
- Full white-labeling
- Upload students in bulk
- Publish interactive videos
- Access to more integrations
- More reporting options, including progress reports, user segments, and course insights reports
- 24/7 premium support

[![LearnWorlds pricing](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-pricing-2023-680x445.png "learnworlds-pricing-2023 – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/learnworlds-pricing-2023.png)

### Pricing, winner: a tie!

Since Teachable has increased its prices in recent years, deciding who offers better value for money is no longer as straightforward.

Teachable offers an attractive free plan for complete beginners, but its more affordable plans limit your course creation immensely.

In contrast, LearnWorlds provides access to unlimited courses and webinars for less, but if it’s a fully white-labeled site you’re after, you’ll end up paying more.

On the other hand, Teachable unlocks white-labeling for cheaper but requires you to move to a higher-priced plan ($309 a month) to access features such as custom reporting, priority support, and advanced theme customization.

### Is LearnWorlds better than Teachable?

It depends on your priorities. LearnWorlds is better for course-creation depth, advanced assessments, and community features, while Teachable is better for simplicity, speed to launch, and native mobile apps. Serious educators tend to prefer LearnWorlds; beginners and people selling varied products tend to prefer Teachable.

### Which is cheaper, LearnWorlds or Teachable?

LearnWorlds Starter is $24 a month and Teachable Starter is $29 a month, both billed annually. For a plan with no transaction fees, Teachable Builder ($69/mo) is slightly cheaper than LearnWorlds Pro Trainer ($79/mo), but LearnWorlds bundles more at that tier. Factor in LearnWorlds’ $5-per-enrollment Starter fee if you sell in volume.

### Does Teachable still have a free plan?

No. Teachable removed its free plan in 2025. You can try any plan free for 7 days, and there is a 30-day money-back guarantee, but there is no longer a permanently free tier.

### Do LearnWorlds and Teachable have mobile apps?

Teachable includes native iOS and Android apps on every paid plan, so students can take courses in a dedicated app. LearnWorlds is browser-based on its standard plans and offers native branded apps only as a separate product.

### Can you migrate from Teachable to LearnWorlds?

Yes. LearnWorlds provides a migration guide and optional done-for-you migration support. Course content transfers over, though items like quizzes, drip schedules, and branding usually need to be recreated manually.

## LearnWorlds vs Teachable: final thoughts

Ultimately, both platforms provide similar services (easy-to-use course creation features, course completion certificates,  SSL certificates included with all their packages, etc.) for similar prices and suffer from similar drawbacks (neither offers much in the way of email marketing or funnel building and both charge hefty transaction fees with their lower-tier plans).

So, all in all, you can’t go too wrong with either. But, there are a few factors to decide on before making your final decision.

[LearnWorlds](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds) is more suited to those further along in their careers. They make it easy to migrate your content to their platform and continue growing your business.

Also, thanks to its community-building features, LearnWorlds really lends itself to building thriving and engaged audiences. Not to mention, the platform boasts powerful video content tools with flexible payment and quizzing options.

[Teachable](https://athemes.com/go/teachable), on the other hand, is a little easier to use and better suited to beginners. Its quizzing functionality isn’t as advanced, but they offer a wide range of building blocks for your courses. However, to unlock full customization with this tool, be prepared to spend a considerable sum on your site every month. In light of that, you may find that migrating to another service such as LearnWorlds as you scale is advisable.

If you’re still not sure, why not give their free trials a shot? This is the best way to test out their interfaces and see which course editor works best for you.

Whichever you decide, we’d love to hear how you get on in the comments box below!

### [How to add titles in a WordPress menu without linking](https://athemes.com/tutorials/wordpress-menu-add-titles-without-linking/)

**Published:** November 4, 2021
**Author:** Sophia Lee

**Content:**

WordPress has a seemingly endless number of customization options for your website. However, figuring out how to apply some of them may not be immediately obvious. One subtle example is adding a title in your menu without linking to a page.

Fortunately, this process can be quick and easy. By adjusting a few options and adding some CSS to your site, you can incorporate titles into your WordPress menu without adding links to go with them.

The steps below work the same with any theme, including [Sydney](https://athemes.com/theme/sydney/), our free business theme used on more than 100,000 sites.

In this tutorial, I’ll cover some of the reasons why you might want to add an unclickable title to your WordPress menu, then I’ll take you through three simple steps to set one up. Let’s go!

#####  Table of Contents 

1. [Why add a title in a WordPress menu without linking to a page](#why-add-a-title-in-a-wordpress-menu-without-linking-to-a-page)
2. [How to add titles in a menu without linking to a page (in 3 steps)](#how-to-add-titles-in-a-menu-without-linking-to-a-page-in-3-steps)
3. [How to add an unlinked title in a block theme](#how-to-add-an-unlinked-title-in-a-block-theme)
4. [Conclusion](#conclusion)

## Why add a title in a WordPress menu without linking to a page

Menus are mostly about making your site [easy to navigate](https://athemes.com/collections/best-wordpress-menu-plugins/). Adding a title without a link may seem counterproductive, but it can be a helpful organizational tool that enables your users to quickly find the information they need.

A major application of this is using an unlinked menu item to categorize sub-items that do have links. For example, here’s a parent title named **Contact Us** that doesn’t link anywhere:

![A sample of a menu where the parent item acts as a title for the linked child items](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Example-No-Link-Menu-Item-e1611871345393.png "Example No Link Menu Item – aThemes")

Instead, **Contact Us** acts as a parent item for the functional child items where users can reach out via email, phone, or by dropping into a brick-and-mortar location. This way, visitors can jump right to their preferred contact method instead of clicking on a link to a contact page and scrolling through all the options.

Unlinked menu titles can also be helpful if you’re looking to display a static message consistently across your site. Even though this method will get the job done, you might be better served by [adding custom header or footer code](https://athemes.com/tutorials/add-header-footer-code-in-wordpress/) if this is your goal.

## How to add titles in a menu without linking to a page (in 3 steps)

Adding titles to a WordPress menu without linking to a page can be a subtle and professional touch. Fortunately, it’s an easy process. Once you know the steps, you’ll be able to quickly add unlinked menu titles wherever you need them.

These steps use the classic menu editor at **Appearance > Menus**, which is available on classic themes. If you use a block theme with full site editing, you won’t see that screen, so skip ahead to the block theme method further down.

### Step 1: Select or create a menu

The first thing you’ll need to do is create or edit the menu you’d like to add an unlinked title to.

You can start by navigating to **Appearance > Menus** in your WordPress dashboard sidebar. This will bring you to the following screen:

![The WordPress Menu Editor](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/wordpress-menu-editor-768x442.png "wordpress-menu-editor – aThemes")

From here, your current menu should already be on the screen if you have one. If you want to start from scratch, click on **create a new menu** instead.

### Step 2: Add a Custom Link

Now that you’ve selected the menu you’re going to work on, you can start creating your unlinked menu title.

Navigate to the **Add menu items** panel on the left side of the screen and open the **Custom Links** tab to expand the options:

![Add custom menu item without linking](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/add-menu-without-link-680x348.jpg "add-menu-without-link – aThemes")

This will display two fields: **URL** and **Link Text**. To make the link unclickable, simply enter **\#** into the **URL** box.

Then, type your unlinked title into the **Link Text** field. In this example, I’ve opted to use the **Contact Us** label.

When you’re done, click on **Add to Menu**. You can add sub-items with links underneath this title if you’d like, and drag and drop menu items to arrange them.

### Step 3: Use CSS to prevent the cursor from changing on hover

The first two steps helped you make a menu item that doesn’t link to a page. However, users who hover over it will still see their cursors change as if they can click on it. As it won’t lead anywhere, you might want to change the cursor for consistency’s sake.

Fortunately, this can easily be done with a little bit of CSS.

In the **Menus** screen, navigate to the upper-right corner and click the **Screen Options** dropdown. This will present you with a few options. Find the one labeled **CSS Classes**:

![The screen options dropdown](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Screen-Options-1-768x235.png "Screen Options – aThemes")

Check this box and close the **Screen Options** menu.

Then, scroll back down to your website’s menu. Locate the title you made earlier that doesn’t have a link.

There should now be an additional field underneath it labeled **CSS Classes (optional)**.

Enter a custom CSS class to correspond with the cursor change (the CSS code will be added next). I’ve used **unclickable** here to keep it simple:

![A menu item with a new CSS class added](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Menus-Screen-with-CSS-Classes-768x521.png "Menus Screen with CSS Classes – aThemes")

After you’ve settled on a class, save your settings.

Then, open the WordPress Customizer by navigating to **Appearance > Customize** in the sidebar menu.

Once you’re there, navigate to the **Additional CSS** tab at the bottom of the menu on the left. Copy and paste the following code:

```
.unclickable > a {
   pointer-events: none;
}
```

The only exception here is if you used a class other than **unclickable** earlier. If you did, just replace that line with whatever name you gave the CSS class.

Your CSS field should then look something like this:

![Code added to the Additional CSS tab of the Customizer](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Additional-CSS-with-Unclickable-Code-e1611871318617.png "Additional CSS with Unclickable Code – aThemes")

The change should be reflected as soon as you’ve entered the additional CSS.

Check that your cursor doesn’t give you the option to click when you’re hovering over your unlinked menu item. Once you’re happy that the changes you’ve made have been implemented, click on **Publish** to save the settings.

After you’ve completed these steps, you should have added a title to your menu without linking it to a page or making it appear clickable at all.

## How to add an unlinked title in a block theme

The steps above use the classic menu editor. If you run a block theme with full site editing, you won’t find Appearance > Menus. Here’s the equivalent with the Navigation block:

1. Go to **Appearance > Editor** to open the Site Editor, then edit the template or template part that holds your navigation (usually the header).
2. Select the **Navigation** block, click the plus (+) to add an item, and choose **Custom Link**.
3. Type your title in the **Label** field. Leave the URL empty (or enter #) so it doesn’t link anywhere, then press Enter.
4. To stop the cursor from changing on hover, add the same CSS (`.unclickable > a { pointer-events: none; }`) through your theme’s Additional CSS or a code plugin.

Not every block theme exposes a CSS-class field on navigation items, so the cursor tweak may need a custom class on a wrapping block or a small CSS rule that targets that menu item directly.

### How do I add a menu item in WordPress without a link?

Go to Appearance > Menus, open the Custom Links panel, enter # (or leave the URL empty) and type your title in Link Text, then click Add to Menu. The item shows as a label without linking anywhere.

### Why do I put # in the URL field?

The # makes the item non-navigational. Left as #, clicking jumps to the top of the current page; removed and left empty, clicking just reloads the page. Either way it works as an unclickable title.

### How do I stop the cursor from changing on hover?

Add a CSS class such as “unclickable” to the menu item, then add the rule .unclickable > a { pointer-events: none; } in Appearance > Customize > Additional CSS or your theme’s CSS.

### How do I do this in a block theme?

Block themes do not have Appearance > Menus. Open the Site Editor (Appearance > Editor), select the Navigation block, add a Custom Link, type the label, and leave the URL empty so it does not link anywhere.

### Can I use an unlinked title as a parent for sub-items?

Yes. A common use is an unlinked parent like “Contact Us” that groups linked child items such as email, phone, and location, so visitors jump straight to the option they need.

## Conclusion

Figuring out how to add a title to your WordPress menu without linking it to a page can be a bit confusing at first. Fortunately, with a little bit of guidance, you can navigate the process with ease.

In this article, I covered three simple steps to add an unlinked title to your WordPress menu:

1. Create or select the menu you’d like to use
2. Add a new Custom Link menu item
3. Apply a few lines of CSS to make the cursor default to a pointer on hover

What unlinked menu option will you create with this tutorial? Let us know in the comments section below!

### [10 Best Kajabi Alternatives 2025](https://athemes.com/collections/kajabi-alternatives/)

**Content:**

[Kajabi](https://athemes.com/go/kajabi) is a popular online course platform for turning your passion into an e-learning business. Like many similar providers, it allows you to sell online courses, subscriptions, and memberships and comes with a few marketing tools to get the word out about your brand.

Whether you’re considering Kajabi to create/host your online courses, or you’ve been using it for a while, you might be looking for alternatives. Maybe you’re on the hunt for a cheaper option? Or, looking for a course builder with more sophisticated quizzing features? Or, do you need a platform that issues course certificates (something that Kajabi doesn’t offer)?

Whatever your reasons, we’ve got you covered. In this article, we’ll discuss the best Kajabi alternatives on the market.

Whichever you pick, if your site runs on WordPress, [Sydney](https://athemes.com/theme/sydney/) is our fast, customizable business theme, with [starter sites](https://athemes.com/sydney-demos/) to build on.

Let’s dive in!

## 1. [Thinkific](https://athemes.com/go/thinkific)

[Thinkific](https://athemes.com/go/thinkific) was built for content creators that needed a simple system for selling online courses. So it’s no wonder it’s one of the most easy-to-use on the market. Thinkific provides everything you need to build, market, and distribute your online courses using a custom web domain.

Thinkific also helps you create a classroom-like learning experience and supports larger organizations that want to develop full-scale online schools.

### Thinkific Key Features

- An incredibly intuitive drag-and-drop editor
- All kinds of media to create courses
- Free video hosting
- Create and customize courses that match your brand
- Publish private and hidden courses and drip-schedule content
- Sell memberships
- Get access to HTML and CSS for complete customization freedom (providing you have the coding know-how)
- Issue course completion certificates

### Thinkific Pros

You can make complex changes to your course’s design by diving into the code. This makes Thinkific one of the most flexible course creation platforms on the market. It’s ideal if you want to achieve a specific look, and you have the coding smarts (or a web developer on your team) to bring your vision to life.

Thinkific also comes with a nifty voice-over feature that allows you to narrate over your presentations.

### Thinkific Cons

Thinkific can be costly, especially if you’re a new business with limited funds. Also, it doesn’t come with any inbuilt marketing tools. You’ll have to use an integration to achieve that sort of functionality.

[![](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/thinkific-768x369.png "thinkific – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/go/thinkific)

### Thinkific Pricing

- **Basic – $39 a month:** Get all Thinkific’s basic course creation features to launch your first course.
- **Pro – $79 a month:** This unlocks site admin permissions and the option of setting assignments, and you can establish student communities within your online school.
- **Premier – $399 a month:** This is best suited for advanced course creators that want to build an education empire.

### Teachable Key Features

- Access to sales analytics
- Email marketing
- An inbuilt affiliate platform where you can create and manage your own affiliate programs

- One-on-one sessions with students
- A Calendly-integration

## Which is the Best Kajabi Alternative for You?

Now, it’s up to you to decide on the best Kajabi alternative for your business. Many people start with a more affordable, user-friendly platform such as Teachable and upgrade to Kajabi later on.

However, certain features are still missing from Kajabi, such as course completion certificates, that might make you choose a different alternative from the get-go and stick with it.

It’s definitely worth reading up on marketplace options such as [Skillshare](https://www.skillshare.com/) and [Udemy](https://athemes.com/go/udemy). Suppose you’re unsure whether course creation is for you. In that case, they offer a risk-free way of dipping your toe in the water before committing to a monthly subscription.

But if you want to create a branded website and start growing your own online community, a fully-fledged learning management software is crucial. In this instance, for their pricing, feature set, and user-friendliness, I recommend [Teachable](https://athemes.com/go/teachable), [Podia](https://athemes.com/go/podia), or [LearnWorlds](https://athemes.com/go/learnworlds).

If you want to create a huge online school (or know that’s what you’re building towards), [Thinkific](https://athemes.com/go/thinkific) might be the way to go.

If you’re looking for a powerful and flexible theme for your booking website, [Kinsley](https://athemes.com/go/kinsley) is a premium option that can help you build an elegant site in no time.

This hotel theme boasts a clean, modern design that can help you promote your accommodation services effortlessly. It’s built with the Elementor page builder plugin, making it easy to customize regardless of your experience level. You can also leverage over 40 custom widgets to create professional pages that deliver a strong user experience.

Kinsley also comes with a ton of features for booking management. These include Automatic Sync, which lets you integrate with various online channels, including Hotels.com, TripAdvisor, Airbnb, and more. You can also utilize room management features, a booking calendar, as well as real-time, smart search availability.

Overall, Kinsley is a feature-rich, flexible hotel theme that is worth checking out regardless of the type of accommodation business you manage.

[More info / Download](https://athemes.com/go/kinsley)

[Demo](https://athemes.com/go/kinsley-demo)

## 7. [WP Rentals](https://athemes.com/go/wp-rentals)

[![](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/WP-Rentals-Booking-WordPress-Theme-768x576.jpg "WP-Rentals-Booking-WordPress-Theme – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/go/wp-rentals)

[WP Rentals](https://athemes.com/go/wp-rentals) lets you list and accept bookings for accommodation, items, and services through your WordPress website.

The booking system that’s integrated into WP Rentals is highly flexible, making it very likely that whatever type of reservations you want to work with, you can configure the system to suit. This includes support for hourly bookings. Pricing can be configured exactly how you want it, with discounts for longer bookings available as well as other options.

WP Rentals also includes a stylish set of frontend online booking forms. These forms can be customized to match the type of bookings you want to make available on your website. Another nice feature of WP Rentals is the ability to enable instant bookings on your website. If you enable this feature for a specific item on your site, then the booking will be placed and secured as soon as it’s submitted by the user.

To help your visitors find the right item they’re looking for, WP Rentals has a powerful search tool. Thanks to the filters and other search features finding the desired options is very straightforward.

[More Info / Download](https://athemes.com/go/wp-rentals) [Demo](https://athemes.com/go/wp-rentals-demo)

## 8. [Travolo](https://athemes.com/go/travolo)

[![](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Travolo-wordpress-theme-680x383.jpg "Travolo wordpress theme – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/go/travolo)

Do you have a tour agency? [Travolo](https://athemes.com/go/travolo) is a booking theme designed specifically for the travel niche.

It has five demos to choose from, with bold and colorful designs and plenty of space for photos. You have a page dedicated to destinations and another one for activities. You can also display your trips and individual trip details on separate pages. The theme was built with Elementor, so it’s easy to customize and it offers a selection of pre-made headers and footers.

Travolo is WooCommerce-ready, enabling you to start selling tours straightaway. Visitors can filter trips by price, destination, duration, activities, and more. Once they select a trip, they can view its full itinerary, check availability on their preferred dates, and then simply proceed to checkout.

Overall, Travolo is the ideal theme for any travel business that sells tours and experiences and wants an efficient booking system.

[More info / Download](https://athemes.com/go/travolo)

[Demo](https://athemes.com/go/travolo-demo)

## 9. [Tripgo](https://athemes.com/go/tripgo)

[![](https://athemes.com/wp-content/uploads/Tripgo-Wordpress-theme-680x383.jpg "Tripgo Wordpress theme – aThemes")](https://athemes.com/go/tripgo)

[Tripgo](https://athemes.com/go/tripgo) is another booking theme built for tour companies. It’s ideal for creating a custom website that reflects your brand.

The Tripgo theme offers six unique demos for travel agencies, plus several different listing layouts for your tours. There’s also a dedicated tour details section, which you can customize with Elementor. For example, you can add a tour plan and display reviews. Other customizable widgets include a tour search bar, customer testimonials, and more.

Additionally, Tripgo uses the Booking Rental plugin. This tool enables you to set up different pricing options based on the time of year and the number of guests. You can also check tour availability, accept deposits, create discount coupons, and a lot more.

With Tripgo, you get full control over the design of your site, as well as the management of your bookings.

[More info / Download](https://athemes.com/go/tripgo)

[Demo](https://athemes.com/go/tripgo-demo)
